relationships.subject: HMGB1
relationships.evidence_quote: macrophage-derived high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1)/receptor for advanced glycation end-products (RAGE) axis, is the upstream signal of the Egr-1/CaV3.2 regulation in sensory neurons of rats with neuropathic pain following L5-SNC

relationships.subject: Egr-1
relationships.evidence_quote: In patch clamp recording experiments, CaV3.2 currents were significantly augmented following Egr-1 overexpression in NG108–15 cells.

relationships.subject: Cdk5
relationships.evidence_quote: Recently, it was reported that Cdk5-dependent phosphorylation of CaV3.2 at serine 561 (Ser561) and 1987 (Ser1987) contributes to enhanced surface expression of the channel [48]

relationships.subject: USP5
relationships.evidence_quote: This leads to enhanced deubiquitination of CaV3.2 channels which protects the channel from degradation, thus augmenting CaV3.2 currents.

relationships.subject: WWP1
relationships.evidence_quote: T-type calcium channels are ubiquitinated by WW Domain Containing E3 Ubiquitin Protein Ligase 1 (WWP1)

relationships.subject: TNF-alpha
relationships.evidence_quote: TNF-α released from immune and epidermal cells in the target tissue of the injured afferents, may also lead to the sensitization of uninjured fibers via transport and accumulation of T-type channels in peripheral nerves [60].

relationships.subject: homocysteine
relationships.evidence_quote: homocysteine enhances the surface expression of CaV3.2 and T-type currents in DRG neurons

relationships.subject: mibefradil
relationships.evidence_quote: Additional studies show that mibefradil also inhibits T-type currents in dissociated dorsal root ganglia (DRG) neurons, stabilizing the channel in the inactive state [22].

key_findings: CaV3.2 expression/activity rises in DRG and dorsal horn across inflammatory and neuropathic pain models and is regulated by ubiquitination (USP5/WWP1), phosphorylation (Cdk5, PKC) and glycosylation.
HMGB1/RAGE/Egr-1 axis drives CaV3.2 upregulation in neuropathic pain; indirect targeting of CaV3.2 regulators is proposed as an analgesic strategy.
